or_east_wall.blurb: East Wall is a sandstone face on Scorpion Buttress in the Callahans, a cluster of cliffs west of Roseburg in southwest Oregon. A steep step a few meters high divides it into a gentler, more featured lower tier and a steeper upper tier. All 17 climbs are sport routes, running from easy fifth-class lines up to about 5.10, with a good number in the 5.6 to 5.9 range, so it suits newer leaders and anyone building mileage. Difficulty tends to climb as you move toward the left side of the wall. A thin band of crumbly shale sits at the base of the step, so a helmet is a sensible idea. Anchors at the top are easy to reach if you want to set a top rope.

or_4_wolf_point.blurb: Wolf Point is a sub-crag of Klinger Spring on the east side of Mt. Hood, in Mt. Hood National Forest. Its 16 routes split between trad and sport, with grades from the 5.7 range to a single 5.12, and the bulk of them in the 5.9 to 5.10 band. The cliff takes its name from bright yellow lichen on the big trees above, and one of the lines follows a prominent arete. It is a handy stop for climbers who want a moderate sport line next to harder trad and sport options. Several of the lines are newer additions, so expect some routes to be less polished than the older classics nearby.

or_brandon_s_cliff.blurb: Brandon's Cliff is the biggest wall in the Willow Creek Canyon climbing area near Madras in central Oregon, reached by a trail up the canyon. Of its 16 routes, most are sport leads and top-ropes, with the grades bunched around 5.10 and a handful of easier and harder lines on either side. Several climbs offer alternate clips or variations that change the grade. The far west end is the best spot for beginners, with gentler routes suited to teaching. The canyon has a wild, out-of-the-way feel and routes carry railroad-themed names, since the cliffs are old rail cuts. A helmet is a good idea in the canyon.

or_north_comb.blurb: North Comb is a steep sport wall in the Honeycombs, a set of small tuff walls and pinnacles on a ridge above the North Umpqua valley in southwest Oregon. The upper wall is a pocketed face, and lower down a rounded, scooped feature holds several bolt lines. All 16 routes are sport, nearly all single pitch with one two-pitch outing, and the grades cluster around 5.9 to 5.10 with a few easier and a couple of 5.11 lines. Pockets and patina give the climbing its character. The trail passes right by the upper wall, so some routes are only steps from the path. Part of the area was affected by fire, which left regrowth in the treetops.

or_f_bomb_shelter.blurb: Bomb Shelter is a tall overhanging wall of dark rock, roughly 75 feet high, at Eagles Rest southeast of Eugene in the Willamette Valley. It sits down and to the right of the Dream Wall, beneath the Sun Deck sector, near the top of the switchback trail. All 16 routes are sport and the character is steep and hard: one easy line aside, almost everything is 5.11 or harder, with a strong run in the 5.13 range. It is a place for projecting and for strong climbers rather than beginners. The wider cliff has mixed rock quality and regular rockfall, so wear a helmet and keep an eye on the base.

or_rusty_point_main.blurb: Rusty Point Main is the first and largest wall you reach in the Rusty Point section of the Lost World cliffs, on the east slope of Mt. Hood. A long fallen fir lying along the base makes a handy bench for belaying. The 16 routes are mostly trad, with a few sport lines and one top-rope, and they mix cracks, faces and aretes. Grades go from about 5.7 to 5.11, with the heaviest concentration at 5.8 and 5.9, which makes it a good intermediate crag. Heavy early traffic left the rock clean and solid. The wall faces west and south, so it holds a bit more shade than neighboring walls.

or_c_dream_wall.blurb: Dream Wall is the left-most big face on the cliff band at Eagles Rest, southeast of Eugene, and the most noticeable sector as you arrive. It is a vertical wall about 50 meters tall with a large arching roof on the right half and a smaller capping roof near the middle. All 15 routes here are sport, and most fall between 5.10 and 5.12, with one easy ramp and a 5.9 for variety. A few lines are multi-pitch. It sits in a clearing beside a large uprooted tree. The cliff overall has variable rock and regular rockfall, so a helmet is recommended.

or_projector_sector.blurb: Projector Sector is a bouldering zone in the Cline Falls area beside the Deschutes River near Redmond, in central Oregon. The boulders ring a small clearing just below the warm-up zone, and three free-standing blocks look as though they were split apart. The 15 problems range widely: several V0 and V1 lines, a middle group around V2 to V3, then a few V5 and V6 and two V10-level projects. Some of the easy problems are slabby with textured holds and can be mossy. Much of the area stays shaded until late afternoon. Bring a couple of pads.
